doc.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Optimism and the Frank Wess recording Surprise, Surprise
summary: He restates his positive view and mentions playing with Frank Wess in Oslo on Surprise, Surprise.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: I sure can. Wonderful. All right, well it’s been really fascinating talking with you.
Oh well it’s been my pleasure, Monk, and I’m glad that you thought of me. I’m very happy, and I hope that I’ve conveyed some kind of message to whoever views this.
Yeah. And I like your positive outlook on the future of jazz too because to be honest with you, not everybody shares it.
Yeah. Some people feel that, well because the venues have changed so much, that there’s just not the places that the talent can be incubated. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Well I find that where there’s a will there’s a way, and that’s the truth. Oh I didn’t mention another great group, a privilege I had of playing with was Frank Wess, who is another fabulous musician of the Basie alumni. And we did a wonderful thing over in Norway, in Oslo. He did a nice recording over there. It’s called “Surprise, Surprise.” We did some stuff of Frank’s writing and a one by Norman Simmons and also Joe Cohn, Al Cohn’s son was on that, and Lynn Seaton. That’s a wonderful CD. And we did some nice things. It was received very well over there. And that’s another way that you could tell that the music is healthy and growing. Of course every time you go somewhere you find out that they’re building, they’re trying to start a little company, a recording company or some kind of a library. I think it’s a healthy atmosphere. I always see something coming up. And there are good musicians out here, and they’re going to get a chance to express themselves. I believe that.
